Consult Summary:
- Adult with known eczema presented with 3–4 days of worsening, widespread pruritic, dry, red rash (chest, hands/arms, especially antecubital fossae). No weeping; has skin cracks. Plan: start fexofenadine and topical Betnovate; continue emollients; follow-up if no improvement or if worsening.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Worsening skin rash with soreness, redness, dryness, and severe itch.
- Distribution: Chest; hands and arms; worst at inner elbows (antecubital areas).
- Onset/duration: Past few days; getting “way worse.”
- Character: Very itchy, dry; cracks present. No weeping reported.
- Modifying factors: Uses emollients (Diprobase cream; “Dermal” shower product) daily; no recent changes. Tried OTC hydrocortisone previously; limited benefit. Previously tried OTC antihistamine (likely cetirizine) without benefit; not currently taking antihistamines.
- Associated symptoms: Denies thickened/darkened skin. No scratch marks despite itching.
- Systems review: Fever and joint pain were queried but not confirmed by patient (not documented).

Past Medical History:
- Eczema (atopic dermatitis): Chronic; historically managed with emollients; prior OTC hydrocortisone use with limited effect. Current flare is more extensive than usual.
- Asthma: Uses blue inhaler intermittently during flares; breathing currently OK per consult. No daily controller noted.

Medications:
- Diprobase cream (emollient); frequency not documented.
- “Dermal” shower emollient; frequency not documented.
- OTC hydrocortisone topical steroid; dose/route/frequency not documented (prior/attempted).
- Blue inhaler for asthma; dose/route/frequency not documented (used PRN).
- Antihistamines: Previously tried OTC (likely cetirizine); currently not taking.
- Prescribed today:
  - Fexofenadine (antihistamine); dose/frequency not documented.
  - Betnovate (topical corticosteroid); advised small amounts (fingertip unit guidance) twice daily for “the next couple of weeks.”

Social History:
- Location: London.
- Smoking/alcohol/substance use: Not documented.
- Other social factors: Not documented.

Family History:
- Mother: Migraine.
- Thyroid disease in mother: Patient stated hypothyroidism; clinician restated hyperthyroidism (conflict noted).

Physical Examination:
- No vitals documented.
- No physical exam findings documented (teleconsult; exam not performed/not recorded).

Investigations:
- None performed or documented.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Atopic dermatitis (eczema) flare, widespread (chest, hands/arms, antecubital fossae); very itchy, dry; cracked skin; no weeping.
  - Start fexofenadine (dose/frequency not documented).
  - Start Betnovate topical; apply small amounts (fingertip unit) twice daily for ~2 weeks.
  - Continue emollients (patient’s “Dermal” wash and emollient cream). Note: Clinician advised to continue “diprovate” (see conflict below).
  - Education: Use thin layer; fingertip unit guidance discussed. Monitor for adverse reactions; seek care if any occur.
  - Follow-up: If worsening before 2 weeks, call earlier; otherwise reassess if no improvement after ~2 weeks. Prescription sent to Boots pharmacy for collection.
- Issue 2: Pruritus secondary to eczema.
  - Management as above with antihistamine (fexofenadine) and topical steroid.
- Issue 3: Asthma, intermittent (blue inhaler PRN).
  - No acute respiratory issues reported. No changes to asthma therapy documented.

General Plan items:
- Continue current emollient regimen; avoid changes until reassessment.
- Return/seek care sooner for worsening symptoms or signs of adverse reaction.

Quality checks (always include at bottom of note, or fill document_quality):
- Missing expected elements: Vitals; comprehensive ROS (fever/joint pain not confirmed); detailed skin exam; exact medication names/strengths/doses/frequencies (fexofenadine dose and Betnovate strength not documented; OTC hydrocortisone specifics not documented; blue inhaler medication unspecified); allergy reconciliation beyond “no drug allergies”; asthma control assessment.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Family history: Patient reported maternal hypothyroidism; clinician restated hyperthyroidism (conflict noted).
  - Emollient name: Patient uses “Diprobase”; later clinician advised continuing “diprovate” (likely misstatement; conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: Some unclear audio/over-talking, incomplete answers, and clinician misstatements; several medication details and ROS elements not clearly confirmed.
